context: Matching of Properly Intersecting Intervals (MI). Buss et al. [13] have observed that ER techniques are effective on what we are calling “Intervals” formulas [4]. The problem is from a competitive programming competition: you are given a sequence a0 , . . . , a2n , initialized as 0s, and a sequence of operations {(li , ri )}i with 0 ≤ li < ri ≤ 2n and 1 ≤ i ≤ n. The operation (li , ri ) assigns value i to all aj with li ≤ j < ri . The goal is to perform each operation exactly once, in any order, to maximize the number of ai such that ai ̸= ai+1 . To encode this as a boolean formula, the problem is reduced to a bipartite maximum matching problem. The problem is then made UNSAT by removing all, but one, right endpoint. A more detailed description can be found in the proceedings of the 2023 SAT Competition [4].
